text: I am more calm now when there is pressure in my work. Before I was getting very nervous and could not sleep before important meetings, now I can tell myself it is only a meeting and the world will not stop. I think the experience give me some distance from my problems.
Ich nehme Belastungen nicht mehr so persönlich und sehe sie eher als Teil des Lebens, der eben dazugehört.

I've lived with chronic back pain for eight years, and the pain itself is one of the most stressful things in my life, along with everything that comes with it: missed work, doctor appointments, people not believing me. The experience happened at a retreat where I went specifically to work on my relationship to the pain. During the ceremony I could feel the pain, but it was just a sensation, it wasn't attached to all the fear and anger. Since then, when I have a bad pain day, I can sometimes remember that and not add the extra layer of panic. I've also become better at saying no to things when I'm in pain, without feeling guilty.
I see things less black and white now, so stressful situations feel less threatening.

Ich habe erkannt, dass mein Stress im Studium vor allem aus meinem eigenen Leistungsdruck kommt und nicht von außen. Ich habe immer gedacht, ich muss die Beste sein, damit meine Eltern stolz sind. In der Erfahrung habe ich gesehen, dass sie mich auch lieben, wenn ich nicht perfekt bin. Seitdem kann ich Prüfungen etwas entspannter angehen.

The experience itself was very challenging. For the first two hours I was convinced I was losing my mind and that I would never come back. My friend who was sitting for me kept reminding me to breathe and that it would pass, and eventually it did. I think that was the most important lesson of the whole thing: even the most terrifying state passes if you breathe and wait. About six months later my best friend from school died in a motorbike accident. It was the worst thing that ever happened to me. I'm sure that before the experience I would have completely fallen apart, I would have started drinking again or just shut down. Instead I somehow had this knowledge in my body that I can get through it, that the pain will move. I let myself grieve, I cried at the funeral, I talked about him with his parents and our friends. I was devastated but I wasn't destroyed, if that makes sense. I think the experience prepared me for that, in a strange way, and I'm very grateful for it.
I started doing cold water swimming and long walks after the experience, and those are my main ways of dealing with stress now. Before it was mostly beer and video games.
Eigentlich ist alles gleich geblieben, was den Umgang mit Stress angeht.

The experience helped me to realise that I'm not lazy or stupid, I probably have ADHD. I got diagnosed a few months later. Since then I handle stressful events better because I ask for help: I told my boss, I use reminders and body doubling with a friend, and I don't hate myself when I forget things.

My son has a severe disability and needs care around the clock. For years I have been exhausted, angry, and grieving the life I thought we would have. I felt that I was failing him and myself. During the experience, I saw my son not as a problem to be solved but as a whole person, with his own joy and his own way of being in the world. I felt an enormous love for him and also a deep acceptance that this is our life. It sounds simple but it changed everything. The stress is still there, the sleepless nights, the fights with the insurance, the hospital visits. But I'm not fighting against reality all the time anymore. I can be with him and enjoy him, and when things are hard, I accept that they're hard and don't add the story that it shouldn't be this way. My wife says I'm more patient and present.
Ich bin ruhiger geworden, wenn es stressig wird. Früher bin ich bei jeder Kleinigkeit explodiert, heute kann ich erst einmal durchatmen und dann reagieren.
The lockdown was hard but I think I coped better than many because I saw it as a temporary phase in a long life.

I work as a nurse in an ICU and the experience showed me how much I've been running on empty, trying to please everyone, patients, doctors, family members. I saw that I was afraid of disappointing anyone. Now when there's a stressful situation, I'm more aware of that fear and I try to remember that I'm allowed to have limits. I've started taking my breaks properly, which sounds tiny but it makes a difference.

Kurz nach der Erfahrung hat sich mein Partner von mir getrennt, nach neun Jahren. Das war ein riesiger Schock. Ich glaube, dass ich ohne die Erfahrung viel schlechter damit umgegangen wäre. Ich hatte während der Erfahrung ein starkes Gefühl, dass das Leben in Wellen verläuft und dass auf jedes Tief auch wieder ein Hoch folgt. Das hat mir geholfen, die Trennung als einen schmerzhaften, aber vorübergehenden Abschnitt zu sehen. Ich habe mir erlaubt, traurig zu sein, ohne mich darin zu verlieren.
I handle stress better and I don't get overwhelmed as fast.

I have borderline personality disorder and I've been doing DBT for some years. The experience made the skills from DBT make sense on a deeper level. Like, I finally understood what radical acceptance means. When I'm in a crisis now I can actually use the skills instead of just knowing about them.

Durch die Erfahrung habe ich gelernt, dass ich in stressigen Zeiten oft dicht mache und niemanden an mich heranlasse. Ich habe in der Erfahrung gesehen, wie einsam mich das macht und wie sehr meine Freunde eigentlich für mich da sein wollen. Ich habe in der Erfahrung auch an meine Großmutter gedacht, die mir immer gesagt hat, dass man über Sorgen reden muss, damit sie kleiner werden. Seitdem versuche ich, das umzusetzen. Als im letzten Jahr meine Firma Insolvenz angemeldet hat und ich meinen Job verloren habe, habe ich sofort mit meinen engsten Freunden darüber gesprochen. Das hat mir sehr geholfen. Ich hatte trotzdem Angst, aber ich war nicht allein damit, und das hat den Unterschied gemacht. Ich habe auch gemerkt, dass ich gar nicht so schwach bin, wie ich immer dachte, sondern dass ich es einfach nicht gewohnt war, mir helfen zu lassen.
I'm more sensitive since the experience. Loud noise, conflict, crowds, all of that stresses me out more than before, and it takes longer to calm down afterwards.
idk, i just dont stress as much about things that i cant change. like whats the point, its gonna happen anyway

Ich pflege seit zwei Jahren meinen Vater, der an Parkinson erkrankt ist. Das ist sehr belastend. Seit der Erfahrung kann ich mit diesen Belastungen ruhiger umgehen. Ich sehe meinen Vater mit mehr Liebe und Geduld und rege mich nicht mehr so auf, wenn etwas schiefläuft. Ich habe auch verstanden, dass ich nicht alles allein schaffen muss, und habe einen Pflegedienst dazugeholt.

I have a deep trust now that everything happens for a reason, or at least that I can find meaning in whatever happens. That has changed how I handle stress completely. Before, I was always anxious about the future, about losing my job, getting sick, being alone. During the experience I felt held by something bigger than me, call it God or the universe, I don't know. I felt that I am part of something that is fundamentally good. Now when something bad happens, I still feel the stress, but underneath it there's this trust. Like when I had to have surgery last year, I was nervous, but I also felt that whatever happened, I'd be okay. It's hard to explain to people who haven't had this kind of experience.
I'm a little better at it maybe. Hard to tell.
Ich nehme Dinge, die ich nicht ändern kann, besser an. Früher habe ich nächtelang gegrübelt, heute sage ich mir, dass ich mein Bestes gebe und der Rest nicht in meiner Hand liegt.

I'm a veteran and I used to react to stress with anger, a lot of anger. During the experience I saw that the anger is a way of not feeling helpless, which is how I felt during my deployment. That insight has helped me a lot. When I feel the anger coming now, I can sometimes stop and recognise that it's the helplessness, and I can talk about that instead.
I talk more openly about my stress with my friends and family instead of keeping it all inside.

Ich mache seitdem bei Stress eine Atemübung, die ich in der Vorbereitung gelernt habe, und gehe öfter in die Natur. Das hilft mir, wieder zur Ruhe zu kommen. Ob das aber an der Erfahrung selbst liegt oder eher an der Vorbereitung, kann ich nicht sagen.

Eighteen months after the experience, I was diagnosed with breast cancer. I was 41. It's the most stressful thing that has ever happened to me and I'm still in treatment. I can honestly say that the experience changed how I've been dealing with it. During the experience, I went through what felt like my own death, and I came out of it with a sense that death is not the enemy, that it's part of the cycle, and that what matters is how we live. When I got the diagnosis, I was terrified, of course. But after the first shock, I found a kind of calm. I decided I would not let the fear take over the time I have, however long that is. I've been very open with my friends and family, and they've carried me through chemo. I've also made peace with the fact that I can't control the outcome. I do my treatments, I eat well, I walk every day, and then I let go. I still have bad days and moments of panic, especially at night, but they pass. I think a lot of that comes from the experience.
Calmer in general, especially with my kids when they're being difficult.
Kann ich nicht genau sagen. Ich hatte seither keine großen Belastungen, und im Alltag merke ich keinen Unterschied. Vielleicht bin ich etwas gelassener, aber das ist schwer einzuschätzen.

I handle conflict in my relationship much better. Before, when my girlfriend and I argued, I would get defensive and say hurtful things, or just walk out. Now I try to listen and understand her side. The experience made me feel so much love for her, and I realised that most of our fights were about small things that didn't matter. We still argue, but it doesn't escalate like before, and we make up quickly.
Much more resilient now, I bounce back faster

Ich sehe belastende Ereignisse heute mehr aus einer Vogelperspektive. Ich frage mich, was ich daraus lernen kann, statt nur zu jammern. Das hat mir bei meinem Umzug in eine neue Stadt sehr geholfen, wo ich am Anfang niemanden kannte.

I stay more relaxed when things go wrong. My car broke down on the highway last month and instead of losing it, I just sat on the side of the road and called for help. My old self would have been shaking.

I've been dealing with OCD and anxiety since I was a teenager, and stressful events always made my symptoms much worse. The experience helped me understand that my compulsions are a way of trying to control uncertainty. Seeing that so clearly gave me a bit of distance. I also started doing ERP therapy after the experience, which I'd been avoiding for years. Now when something stressful happens, I notice the urge to check or count, and I can name it and sit with the discomfort for a while instead of giving in. It's not perfect but I'm handling stress much better.
Ich kann in stressigen Situationen besser ruhig bleiben und behalte eher den Überblick, z.B. bei der Arbeit im Kindergarten.

I've accepted that stress is part of life, not something I can or should avoid. That takes away a lot of the extra stress of being stressed, if that makes sense. When I have a hard week I tell myself: ok, this is a hard week, and that's allowed. I used to think something was wrong with me every time I felt overwhelmed.
Had a hard time with it at first, I was jumpy and anxious for months after

Ich bin seit der Erfahrung viel gelassener im Umgang mit stressigen Situationen. Ich arbeite als Lehrerin, und früher hat mich jeder Konflikt mit Eltern oder Kollegen tagelang beschäftigt. Ich habe nachts wach gelegen und mir überlegt, was ich hätte anders sagen sollen. Heute kann ich solche Situationen besser abhaken. Ich glaube, die Erfahrung hat mir gezeigt, dass ich nicht für die Gefühle anderer verantwortlich bin und dass es in Ordnung ist, wenn nicht alle mit mir einverstanden sind. Ich spreche auch mehr mit meinen Kolleginnen über schwierige Situationen, statt alles mit mir allein auszumachen. Das entlastet mich sehr, und wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig.
I see stress from a different angle now. A lot of what I used to get worked up about seems unimportant compared to the bigger questions about life and death that came up during the experience.
I started journaling and running regularly, both help a lot with stress. I also try to sleep more.
